title: Routing policy conversation kit — draft
body:
Purpose:
Quick, portable reference for field reps to talk through routing policies, model fallback strategies, and cost/latency tradeoffs during discovery and technical conversations. This is intentionally concise — treat it as a pocket deck script + objection cheatsheet.

Audience:
- AEs and SEs during mid-to-late-stage technical calls with platform/infra/ML leads
- SDRs preparing for technical discovery calls

Topline positioning (3 lines):
- Redwood gives you a single API that can route requests by latency, cost, region, or data-sensitivity — not just another model endpoint.
- When capacity or constraints hit, Redwood can transparently fallback to compatible model variants without breaking your UX.
- This reduces downtime risk and gives product teams predictable economics and a clear path for performance tuning.

Key messages to land (short):
- Multi-tier routing: host -> dedicated -> private (VPC); automatic fallbacks across tiers
- Policy types: latency-first, cost-first, region-boundary, data-classification-aware
- Observable outcomes: per-route latency, token-level cost breakdown, and fallback counts in Console

Two-minute demo script (AE -> SE handoff):
1) AE: "We’ll show how routing keeps your app fast even under load." Quick ask: "What SLOs do you target?" (example answer: p99 latency < 300ms for chat).
2) SE: In Console, open the routing policy tab -> show policy creation: target p99, primary model, fallback set, cost cap. Change policy from latency-first to cost-first -> show simulated request stream and delta in estimated cost/latency.
3) AE: highlight that fallbacks are model-compatible (same tokenizer/semantics) and that you can pin versioned rollouts.

Sales scripts and objection handling (short snippets):
- Objection: "We can run this ourselves."
  Script: "Totally — many teams start self-hosting. What customers tell us is that the ops burden and inconsistent latency under traffic is the blocker. Redwood handles optimized kernels, autoscaling, and automated fallbacks so product velocity and SLAs are predictable."
- Objection: "Won’t fallback change output quality?"
  Script: "Good question. We recommend a graded fallback strategy: first fallback to a same-family quantized replica (negligible quality delta), then to a smaller family only if needed — and Redwood provides regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets so you see any quality shifts immediately."
- Objection: "Pricing will spike with dedciated capacity."
  Script: "We show per-route token economics in Console; you can route cold traffic to lower-cost variants and reserve Dedicated capacity for steady peak tiers. Our Optimize suggestions often cut unit cost by ~20% for typical chat workloads (customer specific)."

Mini decision table (talking points):
- If customer priority = latency-critical -> recommend Dedicated + latency-first routing + prefix/KV cache
- If priority = cost-sensitive -> recommend Hosted + cost-first routing + aggressive caching/quantization profiles
- If priority = regulatory/data isolation -> Private deployment + region-boundary policies and KMS integration

Example quick numbers (ballpark, for conversational framing only):
- Hosted baseline model: ~ $0.0007 / token (illustrative), p95 latency 120–220ms in us-west
- Dedicated (reserved GPUs): capacity pricing depends on commit; unit economics typically improve 15–40% as throughput stabilizes
- Typical customer win: reduce 90th percentile latency by 2x during peak vs naive self-hosting due to batch/kv optimizations

Small checklist for AE/SE before pilot kickoff:
- Capture SLOs (p50/p95/p99) and peak qps
- Define acceptable quality delta for fallback model(s) and list eval prompts
- Agree on data residency and KMS needs
- Identify traffic routing policy (latency/cost/region) and fallback hierarchy
- Add Slack channel + Console invitation for pilot monitoring

Open questions / work to-do (internal):
- Need one-pager comparing common fallback chains (same-family FP16 vs quantized vs smaller-family) with expected quality delta and cost delta. Owner: Marco.
- Add a short recorded demo (2–3 mins) showing policy flip in Console and fallback live — annotate with talking points. Owner: Rae.

Example quick links to show during calls:
- Console routing policies: Console -> Observability -> Routing (show policy create)
- Eval regression alert sample: Confluence/QA -> Eval-regressions page (link in linked_artifacts)

Tone guidance for reps:
- Keep it concrete and numbers-oriented for infra/platform buyers.
- For product/PMs, lean into UX continuity (how fallbacks preserve session state / KV cache).
- For procurement, emphasize predictable unit economics and reserved capacity discounts.

Notes to self (choppy):
- rehearse demo flip: latency-first -> cost-first and simulate spike
- capture screenshots for one-pager
- confirm example ballpark numbers with pricing ops before public use

End of kit — this doc lives as a lightweight companion to the longer "routing policies" playbook. Use often, iterate fast when we collect field examples.
